To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
subchronic preexposures to CO modify the heart response to a challenge with CO + a low dose of isoproterenole in rats.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of repeated intermittent CO exposures on the heart and ECG response to an acute combined challenge with CO and a sympathomimetics.
the effects of intermittent exposure to a relatively low CO concentration (500 ppm) on the response to an acute CO+isoproterenol exposure.

a model of a combined challenge of the heart with a low dose sympathomimetic drug and a sublethal dose of a gaseous pollutant, which is a more realistic situation in the case of a chronic exposure to CO than a single high dose.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of preexposure to CO on the heart response to an acute combined challenge of CO and isoproterenolic is complex and depends on a number of factors, some of them being not yet identified.
preexposure to CO modifies heart response to an acute combined challenge of CO and isoproterenal, the effect being primarily attributable to the hematological changes.
the preexposure to CO modifies the heart response to an acute challenge with CO and sympathomimetic drug, but that the mechanism of this modification is complex and not fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the preexposed rats were more resistant to a combined challenge with a low dose isoproterenolo and CO, as compared to the control group.

the heart of the rat exposed to CO for a short period is not only a sensitive target organ but also a sensitive indicator of CO exposure, especially when combined with a low isoproterenolic challenge.
the preexposure to CO modifies the ECG pattern and arrhythmias induced by the combined challenge with isoproterenal and CO.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ECG changes in the heart during the combined CO + isopreterenol challenge are a function of both CO and the sympathomimetic drug.
the heart response to CO exposure is not only dependent on COHb, but is also influenced by other factors.

repeated exposure to CO induces adaptive changes in the cardiovascular system, which may be beneficial for the heart during subsequent CO exposure, but the mechanisms underlying this phenomenon remain to be clarified.
